newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B indices end up encouraged by A shares.
newsitem.headline: China's B indices end up encouraged by A shares.

text.p: China's B share indices closed up on Wednesday in line with rises on the A share markets due to buying on shares with expectations of good results for 1996, brokers said.
Shanghai's B share index gained 0.511 points or 0.82 percent to 63.167 points and Shenzhen's B index rose 2.45 points or 1.68 percent to close at 148.23 points.
The A share index in Shanghai climbed 14.089 points or 1.45 percent to 984.078 points while Shenzhen's A index rose 5.66 points or 1.62 percent to end at 355.88.

Shenzhen brokers said investors were encouraged by one A share firm, Hainan Minyuan, which reported that its audited net earnings for 1996 had surged dramatically to 485.29 million yuan, against 1995's 375,704 yuan.
"Market sentiment was boosted by the report and it fuelled buying interest in other issues likely to post good results for last year," a broker with a major Chinese brokerage said.
On the Shanghai B share market, investors were encouraged by rises among the A shares in the afternoon session, brokers said.
Textile machinery maker Erfangji was the star on speculative buying, rising $0.008 or 5.63 percent to $0.150 on volume of 26,000 shares.
Market giant Shanghai Tyre followed on institutional support, brokers said. It ended up $0.020 or 4.46 percent to $0.468 on volume of 854,500 shares.

Blue chip Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor was the most active share on heavy institutional selling on investors' jitters over its results, but bargain-hunting was also active after sharp losses in the past few days, brokers said.
It ended flat at $0.486 on volume of 3.3 million shares.
Meanwhile, on the Shenzhen bourse, all 43 Shenzhen-listed B shares traded and gained on Wednesday.
Fiyta, the biggest gainer, rose HK$0.32 or 5.61 percent to HK$6.02 on volume of 477,724 shares due to investor confidence over the Shenzhen-based watch maker's 1996 results, brokers said.
Beverage maker Shenbao, Tuesday's biggest loser, rallied HK$0.22 or 4.68 percent to HK$4.92.
China Bicycle was the most active share on volume of 1.92 million shares and climbed HK$0.13 to HK$3.98 due in part to investor confidence in its earnings outlook, brokers said.
In Shanghai's A share market, United Agriculture was the star on institutional buying, surging 0.71 yuan or 10 percent to its limit-up of 7.81 yuan on volume of 1.0 million shares.

In Shenzhen's A share market, bulldozer manufacturer Shandong Shantui Engineering Machinery, which listed 88.60 million A shares and 12.50 million staff shares on Wednesday, ended at 9.28 yuan on the heaviest volume of 77.75 million shares.
The A shares were issued on the Shenzhen bourse last month at 4.28 yuan each. The staff shares were offered at 1.20 yuan each in 1993.
Guangzhou Dongfang Hotel closed at its 10 percent limit-up of 8.24 yuan. There had been widespread talk the hotel's 1996 net earnings would be better than expected, brokers said.
